title: Turn biology questions into interactive cited diagrams
summary: A developer built Anima, an add-on that has Claude Code turn biology questions into interactive, sourced diagrams; they've published live examples on dopamine, stimulants, semaglutide and nerve cells.
agent_role: Claude sizes the job, collects sources, builds the standalone HTML figure, and checks it zoomed in, in both themes and at phone width. The human writes the request and reviews the result.
outcome: The author publishes live figures on dopamine receptors, stimulants, addiction circuits, semaglutide, estrogen and myelinated neurons.
what_they_did: The developer Garinmckayl built Anima, a reusable instruction set for Claude Code. It turns a biology question into a standalone interactive diagram, such as how cocaine and amphetamine act on dopamine. Claude gathers sources and pulls real molecule drawings from PubChem, a public chemistry database. It adds switches that change the diagram, then checks the page zoomed in, in light and dark modes, and on phone screens.
how_it_went: The author has published live diagrams made this way. Topics include dopamine receptors, stimulants, reward and addiction, semaglutide, estrogen and aggression, and a nerve cell with its insulating coating. Each diagram lists its sources.
worth_knowing: Numbers that can't be checked are left out. Drug diagrams explain how the drug works only, with no doses or ways of taking it, and are for learning, not medical advice.
prompt: /anima show [biological subject and mechanism] for [audience], with a [toggle or slider, e.g. inhibitor on/off] that changes the mechanism. Collect sources before drawing. Cite every number with its species, conditions and units, and leave out anything you cannot verify. Separate what is established from what is one leading model. Output a standalone HTML page in dark and light themes with an educational-use note. Then check it zoomed in, in both themes and at phone width.

curation.rationale: An original science-communication workflow with a live gallery of finished figures, strict sourcing rules, evals and a reviewer-style self-check. The score includes a small boost for being a non-coding entry.
